terminal_findings.mechanism: Latest-occurrence projection could suppress an earlier unresolved material occurrence.
terminal_findings.precondition: A lineage contains an unresolved material occurrence.
terminal_findings.event: A later same-key occurrence is classified non-material without explicit resolution.
terminal_findings.observable_failure: The concern appears neither open nor resolved in terminal output.
terminal_findings.falsifier: A sticky-open test shows the lineage remains open until explicit targeted resolution.

terminal_findings.mechanism: Ungrouped quarantine could detach a correction from its revision provenance.
terminal_findings.precondition: A valid same-mechanism occurrence is falsely rejected by identity validation.
terminal_findings.event: A corrected occurrence later enters the group without projected quarantine provenance.
terminal_findings.observable_failure: The grouped audit view cannot explain the correction's origin.
terminal_findings.falsifier: Immutable bidirectional correction links and grouped provenance are traversable while remaining terminal-inert.

terminal_findings.mechanism: The axis-and-mechanism group key was treated as semantic concern identity.
terminal_findings.precondition: A failure-handler revision creates two distinct concerns under the same group key.
terminal_findings.event: Resolution evidence targets only one concern.
terminal_findings.observable_failure: Both concerns are falsely closed or remain undifferentiated.
terminal_findings.falsifier: Two same-key concern lineages retain separate open and resolved statuses when only one is resolved.

terminal_findings.mechanism: A retained mechanism ID may mask material mechanism replacement.
terminal_findings.precondition: No explicit mechanism-identity contract defines continuity across revisions.
terminal_findings.event: The handler or mechanism changes while retaining its ID.
terminal_findings.observable_failure: Distinct mechanisms or concerns may be falsely deduplicated.
terminal_findings.falsifier: Contract-backed replacement and retention tests classify mechanism continuity deterministically.

terminal_findings.mechanism: An apparently valid but erroneous concern-lineage assignment can silently split or merge concerns.
terminal_findings.event: An occurrence is assigned to the wrong lineage without triggering ambiguity handling.
terminal_findings.observable_failure: Terminal statuses silently merge unrelated concerns or split one concern.
terminal_findings.falsifier: Adjudication tests detect and correct apparently valid erroneous lineage assignments.

terminal_findings.mechanism: Equivalent concerns with different mechanism IDs remain separated.
terminal_findings.event: Occurrences are grouped strictly by axis and mechanism ID.
terminal_findings.observable_failure: One concern is reported as multiple findings.
terminal_findings.falsifier: A demonstrated cross-ID equivalence case is correctly reconciled without false merging.

terminal_findings.mechanism: Immutable quarantine and provenance records accumulate.
terminal_findings.precondition: Malformed or corrected records persist for auditability.
terminal_findings.event: Repeated revisions generate quarantined records and links.
terminal_findings.observable_failure: Storage and human review load grow without a demonstrated operational bound.
terminal_findings.falsifier: Measured accumulation and review evidence demonstrates acceptable resource behavior.

limitations: Core-only fixed-three-v1 run used three real separate threads: Proposing TL, Peer TL, and Chief Architect; no specialists or retries were used.
Peer received no proposal or preferred outcome before its first inspection. Chief was pre-reserved but received no proposal, debate history, or preferred outcome before the terminal packet.
The closed-world case provides no mechanism-identity contract or lineage-adjudication evidence; the Chief deferred pending those named gates.
R2 false separation and R4 audit/storage overhead remain open accepted limitations; acceptance does not mark them resolved.
